correctness.rationale: For independent Poisson-thinned edges, each unmarked indicator is a product of \(d\) Bernoulli\(q\) indicators. Two vertices share one indicator exactly when adjacent, proving both moments. Conditioning a uniformly chosen vertex to be unmarked gives a monotone size-biased coupling; its exact excess expectation \(p[1+d(q^{-1}-1)]\) and the Poisson Stein factor prove the explicit uniform TV bound. Monotonicity of \(d(e^{u/d}-1)\) yields \(O_x(n^{-1/2})\) for every \(d\ge2\). The no-unmarked event yields Gumbel; independent Poisson interarrival times de-Poissonize. Two-sided integrable tails give the Euler-constant correction. Degree one exactly reduces to an \(n/2\)-type coupon collector. Replayed standard-library verifier passed 593 checks; no finite enumeration substitutes for proofs. Assumptions and ranges are explicit.

originality.rationale: The theorem concerns a graph-uniform Gumbel law, graph-uniform \(O(n^{-1/2})\) Poisson error, exact second moments, and an optimal degree-one boundary for uniformly sampled graph edges. Betken–Thäle 2022/2023 treats all equally probable fixed-size groups, not sparse edge supports; Schilling–Henze 2021 permits near-uniform probabilities per group, not absent pairs; Falgas-Ravry–Larsson–Markström 2016/2020 supplies general first-order concentration rather than the stated limit and rate. A comparison with a related mathematical result found an edge-coupon limit driven by divergent degree-one/degree-two sets; that implication excludes the d>=3 regular regime. Search is not uniqueness proof; general or unindexed group-coupon approximation remains the material risk.
residual_risks: A general unindexed Poisson approximation for sparse dependent fixed-size coupon supports might subsume the result.
The standard size-bias inequality is classical; only the graph-specialized uniform conclusion and boundaries are asserted as the new contribution.
No independent exhaustive historical-priority audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Uniformly selected graph edges are a natural sparse-support group coupon process. A topology-independent centered Gumbel profile, explicit finite-graph variance and a universal quantitative Poisson rate uniformly over all degrees at least two materially strengthen known first-order coverage concentration and distinguish degree one as a sharp structural boundary. This is a theorem over arbitrary disconnected regular graph sequences, not a fixed example or generic restatement of fully uniform group collection.
